# Start work in the right directory

## Problem statement

When `wl ampa start-work` provisions and enters a *fresh* dev container, the
interactive shell is started with an explicit `cd` to the container-local
sandbox path (`/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`) instead of the canonical
`/workdir/project` symlink. Any already-claimed container is re-entered with
`cd /workdir/project`, so the initial entry is inconsistent with re-entry,
confuses the shell prompt (it computes its relative path against
`/workdir/project`), and makes tooling or user commands that assume
`/workdir/project` report the wrong location.

## Users

- **AI agents** launched into a container by `wl ampa start-work`: they expect
  the project to be at `/workdir/project` so scripts, prompts and `wl ampa
  finish-work` resolve consistently.
- **Operators** reviewing/spawning sandboxes: they expect the documented
  `/workdir/project` path to hold regardless of whether the container was just
  created or re-entered.

### Example user stories

- As an AI agent, when I am dropped into a fresh dev container, I want to be in
  `/workdir/project` so that relative paths, the prompt and tooling match every
  other entry point.
- As an operator, when I run `wl ampa start-work <id>` and then `pwd`, I want to
  see `/workdir/project`, not a `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl ampa start-work <work-item-id>` (and its `sw` alias) starts the
  interactive shell in `/workdir/project` for a newly-provisioned container,
  i.e. `pwd` inside the container reports `/workdir/project` (verification:
  manual E2E `wl ampa sw <id>` then `pwd`).
- [ ] Initial entry is consistent with the already-implemented re-entry and
  legacy-container paths, which both `cd /workdir/project` (verification: code
  inspection + assertion that all interactive entry commands reference
  `/workdir/project`).
- [ ] The shell prompt's relative-path segment resolves against
  `/workdir/project` (no leading `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` shown) and
  `/etc/ampa_bashrc` continues to `cd /workdir/project` (verification: manual
  E2E prompt check).
- [ ] An automated regression test asserts that the interactive entry command
  changes into `/workdir/project` and not the container-local
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` path; the test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes after the fix (verification: `npm test` /
  `node --test` in the ampa project).
- [ ] Behaviour of `wl ampa finish-work` and the `--wait` / re-entry flows is
  unchanged (verification: existing ampa test suite green).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The container project is physically cloned to
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`; `/workdir/project` is a symlink to it
  created by the setup script. The fix must not move the physical clone.
- Must keep the existing pool/template provisioning, `wl sync` and prompt
  behaviour intact.
- Change is confined to the ampa plugin's `startWork` entry command; the ampa
  project is the implementation repository (see open questions).

## Existing state

- The `start-work` implementation moved out of this repository: the
  `skill/install-ampa/` skill and `ampa.mjs` plugin now live in the **ampa**
  repository (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/ampa.git`), under
  `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs`. It was removed from SorraAgents in
  commit `ae0d8474` ("install_ampa skill is now in the ampa proejct itself",
  2026-04-10); the `ampa-repo` git submodule pointer was also removed.
- The container setup clones to `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` and
  creates the symlink `/workdir/project` → that path; `/etc/ampa_bashrc` already
  ends with `cd /workdir/project`.
- Re-entry paths (`start-work` on a claimed pool container / legacy
  `ampa-<id>`) use `cd /workdir/project 2>/dev/null; … exec bash --login`.
- The initial interactive entry in `startWork` used
  `cd ${containerProjectRoot} && exec bash --login` (the `/tmp` path).
- **A fix already exists in the ampa repository on `origin/dev`**: commit
  `77856e0` ("fix: use canonical /workdir/project in start-work initial entry
  (SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW)") changes that one line to
  `cd /workdir/project && exec bash --login`. The matching branch is
  `wl-SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW-fix-start-work-directory`. It is **not yet on
  `main`** (normal dev→main release flow) and the local ampa `dev` checkout is
  one commit behind `origin/dev`.
- The fix commit contains **no automated test** and has not updated the manual
  E2E expectations.

## Desired change

Enter a freshly-provisioned dev container in the canonical
`/workdir/project` directory, matching the re-entry paths, and add regression
coverage so the initial-entry path cannot silently diverge again.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` (ampa repository) — `startWork()`
  initial interactive entry (`distrobox enter … -c 'cd /workdir/project &&
  exec bash --login'`, currently line ~2137 on the fix branch). Also
  `buildContainerSetupScript()` / `/etc/ampa_bashrc` writer if the canonical
  path is factored out.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs` (ampa repository) — add/extend a
  regression test for the entry command.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-start-work-template-escape.mjs` (ampa repository) —
  nearby start-work setup-script assertions if the path is interpolated.
- `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` (ampa repository) — manual E2E
  expectations / documentation of `/workdir/project`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the ampa repository, since that is where
  `start-work` lives today; the SorraAgents reference in the commit message is
  the originating work-item ID.
- **Risk:** adding an automated test may require refactoring the entry command
  out of `startWork` into a small exported helper (the command is currently
  built inline and spawned directly), otherwise it is only testable via the
  manual E2E script. Mitigation: extract a pure helper (e.g.
  `buildEntryCommand(cName)`) and unit-test it.
- **Risk:** local ampa `dev` is behind `origin/dev`; implementing from the local
  checkout without pulling would recreate/conflict with the existing fix.
  Mitigation: start from the fix branch / `origin/dev`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** while in the entry code it is tempting to refactor the
  pool/template or prompt logic. Any such extra opportunity should be recorded
  as a separate linked work item, not folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLQ8Z6V20C2FPFP** — "start-work Subcommand" (completed) — defines the
  `wl ampa start-work` behaviour this work item corrects.
- **SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O** — "Podman development container for SorraAgents"
  (completed) — parent epic; origin of the `/workdir/project` convention.
- **SA-0MLRGE8T01IHS922** — "When run wl ampa sw do a wl sync" (completed) —
  the `wl sync` behaviour on entry/re-entry, adjacent to this flow.
- **SA-0MLQ8ZT1300Q1MOM** — "list-containers Subcommand" (completed) — related
  container lifecycle command.
- ampa repository commit `77856e0` on `origin/dev` — the existing fix.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The `start-work` code now lives in the ampa repository
  (`SorraTheOrc/ampa`), and the fix for this work item is already committed
  there on `origin/dev` (`77856e0`, referencing SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW), not yet on
  `main`. Should this SorraAgents work item (a) be closed as complete,
  documenting the ampa fix, (b) be migrated/copied to the ampa project's
  worklog (prefix `AM`), or (c) keep additional work in SorraAgents?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the SA implement skill runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree, where the ampa plugin no longer exists, so an
  implementer cannot make the change here without editing another repository.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The ampa fix is a one-line change with no automated
  regression test. Should this work item also add a test asserting the initial
  entry `cd`s to `/workdir/project` (which likely requires extracting the entry
  command into a testable helper), or is manual E2E coverage sufficient?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: no existing test asserts the
  entry command; `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` documents the path but
  is not automated.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** If the fix is accepted as already complete, should the
  SorraAgents work item still record the ampa commit hash/PR and be closed once
  the fix reaches ampa `main`, or closed immediately against `origin/dev`?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the global workflow normally

# Review find-related skill

## Problem statement

The find-related skill was reported as slow and verbose (SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9). This task reviews whether the v3 improvements have adequately addressed these concerns and whether further improvements are warranted.

## Existing state

The find-related skill underwent a major v3 overhaul (SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9) that addressed two root causes:

**Speed**: v2 had a per-keyword subprocess fan-out problem (523 keywords → 523 `wl search` spawns at ~0.5s each → ≥240s timeout). v3 caps worklog search to the top 8 frequency-ranked keywords (one subprocess each), reducing search from 523 spawns to 8 (~4s). The feedback loop (where the automated report's tokens fed back into keyword extraction, growing from 14 → 82 → 523) was closed by stripping the report section before keyword extraction.

**Verbosity**: v2's report included raw keyword lists (58% of report bloat) and scanned `.worklog/` (83% of scanned files, including stale worktree clones and the skill's own sidecar report). v3 caps matched keywords per file at 5 with a `(+N more)` marker, excludes `.worklog` from repo scans, and uses deterministic section boundaries for idempotency.

**Measured improvements**:
- Wall-clock: ≥240s (timeout) → ~3s
- Subprocesses: 523 → 8
- Repo scan files: 2,188 → 362 (83% reduction)
- Keywords: 523 (unbounded) → 8 (capped at MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS)
- Report duplicates on re-run: stacked `###` blocks → single atomic replacement

## Assessment

The v3 changes directly address the original concerns about speed and verbosity. The skill now:
- Runs in ~1-3s for typical work items
- Produces compact, deterministic reports
- Is idempotent across re-runs
- Excludes non-authoritative directories from scans

- [ ] Confirm the v3 improvements have been merged and deployed
- [ ] Verify the skill runs in <5s on representative work items
- [ ] Verify reports are compact and useful (no verbose keyword dumps)
- [ ] Verify idempotency (re-runs produce identical output)

- **Assumption**: The v3 changes have been fully merged. Verify via commit history.

# Audit Skill Improvements: P1–P3 Optimization Backlog

## Problem Statement

The audit skill (`skill/audit/`) has accumulated correctness gaps, performance issues, and code-quality debt from prior feature additions. This epic coordinates the systematic resolution of critical and high-priority defects followed by medium-priority refactors and polish.

## Users

- **Map (agent):** Executes `/skill:audit` on work items and expects fast, correct, reproducible audits.
- **Ralph (orchestrator):** Consumes persisted audit reports (`skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`) to gate merge approvals.
- **Developers:** Review audit output and fix flagged issues; they rely on audit accuracy.

> **User stories (derived from children):**
> 1. As a developer, I want the audit to detect uncommitted working-tree changes so it does not produce stale verdicts.
> 2. As an operator, I want audit `wl` calls to resolve the worklog store efficiently (cached, not per-call sibling scan).
> 3. As an orchestrator, I want the audit SKILL.md to stay under ~13 KB so it fits in context windows.
> 4. As a developer, I want the audit runner to execute faster by avoiding redundant `wl show` fetches and consolidating duplicate parsers.
> 5. As a reviewer, I want the test suite to be split by concern for faster iteration and clearer failure diagnostics.

## Summary

**Bug (stale-audit correctness gap).** `_compute_content_fingerprint` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, ~line 696) fingerprints only: git HEAD sha + work-item description hash + Key Files list. However, the audit's own file-scope manifest reads `git status --porcelain` (untracked/modified files) and the deep-analysis model reads the **working tree**, not just HEAD. So uncommitted code changes between audits do **not** invalidate freshness — the freshness gate can serve a stale audit for code that has since changed.

The docs claim "a change in ANY fingerprint component invalidates freshness", but working-tree state is not a component.

## Expected behaviour

Include the working-tree state in the fingerprint payload: a hash of `git status --porcelain` + `git diff --name-only HEAD` output (sorted, deterministic). A change in any uncommitted file, untracked file, or commit invalidates freshness; an untouched repo keeps the same fingerprint.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Modifying an uncommitted tracked file invalidates the fingerprint (stale audit → re-run).
2. Adding an untracked file invalidates the fingerprint.
3. Committing a change also invalidates (via the existing HEAD sha component).
4. An untouched working tree + unchanged description + unchanged Key Files keeps the same fingerprint (freshness preserved).
5. Unit tests cover all four cases; `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` passes green.

## Summary

`skill/audit/SKILL.md` lines 22–24 document a "Pre-flight affirmation": "Verify absence before proceeding to the audit flow. Confirm that the work item is ready for audit and that no active conflicting processes exist." **No code implements this.**

# Audit freshness gate: re-audit only when files touched by the work item changed

## Problem statement

The audit freshness gate (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` —
`_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint`) keys freshness on a
whole-repo git HEAD sha plus a whole-repo working-tree hash. Any commit or
working-tree change anywhere in the repository — even one that touches files
completely unrelated to the audited work item — changes the fingerprint and
forces an expensive full two-phase re-audit. This produced a real false
re-audit: `NV-0MSP7P2PN009FT9U` was audited "Ready to close: No" (AC5 partial)
with a byte-identical content fingerprint on re-audit, yet an operator
`/skill:audit` invocation re-ran the full pipeline (twice: dry-run then
persisted) and the final persisted verdict flipped to "Ready to close: Yes"
purely from model judgment variance on the same unverifiable AC — no new
evidence. A freshness gate that asserted "the files this item touched are
unchanged" would have returned the stored verdict.

## Users

- **Operator running `/skill:audit <id>`** on an item whose work files are
  unchanged — I want the stored verdict returned in seconds so unrelated repo
  commits never trigger an expensive re-audit.
  - As an operator, I want the gate to be strict about the work item itself:
    any change to files the item touched (or to its ACs/description/Key Files)
    must invalidate freshness.
- **Auditing agent / parent-audit runner** reusing child verdicts — I want the
  child content gate to stop being invalidated by unrelated commits, so parent
  audits no longer re-audit children whose own work is untouched.
- **Maintainer of the audit pipeline** — I want the freshness semantics and
  their fail-open/fail-stale trade-offs documented and unit-tested.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **(AC1)** Freshness is decided from the work item's touched-file set, not
  the bare repo HEAD sha: a commit that touches only unrelated files does
  **not** invalidate a stored audit whose per-path fingerprint is unchanged.
- [ ] **(AC2)** Any change to a file in the touched-file set (committed or
  uncommitted) invalidates freshness and re-runs the pipeline.
- [ ] **(AC3)** Work-item description / AC / Key Files changes still invalidate
  freshness (existing behaviour preserved).
- [ ] **(AC4)** Touched-file resolution falls back to fail-open (re-run the
  pipeline) when it cannot be determined (no recorded commits, git
  unavailable).
- [ ] **(AC5)** Tool-artifact rewrites (e.g. Unity `ProjectSettings` churn from
  batch runs — Nova `AGENTS.md` pitfall #4) are handled explicitly: either
  excluded from the touched-file comparison or documented as
  always-invalidating, with a test covering the chosen behaviour.
- [ ] **(AC6)** Unit tests cover: unrelated-commit freshness (AC1), touched-file
  change invalidation (AC2), description-change invalidation (AC3), and
  fail-open fallback (AC4).
- [ ] **(AC7)** A regression test reproduces the `NV-0MSP7P2PN009FT9U`
  scenario — a second audit at unchanged touched-file state returns the stored
  verdict without re-running the pipeline (no model calls).
- [ ] **(AC8)** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, and
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.
- [ ] **(AC9)** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Read-only, deterministic fingerprint.** The gate must remain cheap and must
  never mutate the repository or the work item.
- **Fail-open on indeterminacy, fail-stale on change.** If the touched-file set
  or per-path hashes cannot be resolved, the gate must return "not fresh" and
  re-run (never return a stale verdict). Being stale is never wrong, only
  wasteful; being fresh when the work changed is a correctness bug.
- **Backward compatibility.** Legacy audits persisted without a fingerprint
  must keep using the existing 60 s time gate
  (`AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS`), and the persistence-write tolerance
  (`AUDIT_PERSIST_WRITE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS`) must be preserved.
- **Bounded cost.** Touched-file resolution must not add unbounded git calls —
  one `git log` + one per-path `rev-parse`/`log -1` per touched path is the
  expected budget; no full-repo blob hashing.
- **Interaction with SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ.** The currently-shipped whole-repo
  working-tree hash must be narrowed to the touched-file set (or the
  working-tree component dropped) so unrelated uncommitted changes no longer
  invalidate freshness, while the stale-audit correctness property it was
  added for is retained for touched files.
- **Checkpointing unaffected.** Phase checkpointing (SA-0MT6EZUS9004FJ9T) still
  keys on git HEAD sha; the freshness change must not break checkpoint
  resume/clear semantics.

## Existing state

- `_compute_content_fingerprint` (`audit_runner.py` ~L1384) builds a JSON
  payload of `{head_sha, description_hash, key_files, working_tree_hash}` and
  sha256-hashes it. `head_sha` comes from `_resolve_audited_head` (`git
  rev-parse HEAD`); `working_tree_hash` from `_resolve_working_tree_hash`
  (whole-repo `git status --porcelain` + `git diff --name-only HEAD`).
- `_check_audit_freshness` (~L1256) extracts the stored fingerprint from the
  persisted report (`Audit content fingerprint: <sha256hex>`) and compares it
  with the freshly computed one; equal ⇒ serve the stored `rawOutput`, else
  re-run. Missing/uncomputable fingerprint ⇒ fail open (return `None`).
- The same content gate is used for child-verdict reuse in
  `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~L4983) and in several other call sites
  (`cmd_issue`, base-freshness guard, batch paths).
- `_extract_key_files` (~L3892) already parses the `## Key Files` section from
  the work item description.
- Tests live in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (~881
  lines) covering HEAD-sha changes, description changes, Key Files changes,
  working-tree changes, legacy time gate, and force bypass.
- Documentation of the current semantics: `skill/audit/SKILL.md` L121 and
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` L231, L455, L605.

## Desired change

Replace the whole-repo HEAD/work-tree fingerprint with a **per-work-item
touched-file fingerprint**:

1. **Resolve the touched-file set** as the union of:
   (a) files in commits that reference the work item id
   (`git log --all --grep=<id> --name-only`, plus commit hashes recorded in the
   item's comments by the implement skill);
   (b) the `Key Files` entries parsed from the description (`_extract_key_files`).
   Normalise, de-duplicate, and sort the resulting path list.
2. **Fingerprint payload**: for each touched path, capture its current state —
   either `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` (blob hash) or `git log -1 --format=%H --
   <path>` (latest commit touching the path) — plus the per-path working-tree
   diff state (narrowed `git status --porcelain -- <paths>` /
   `git diff --name-only HEAD -- <paths>`). The payload is
   `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}`. The whole-repo `head_sha` is
   removed.
3. **Freshness check**: recompute the payload; equality ⇒ fresh (return the
   stored report), inequality ⇒ stale (re-run).
4. **Fail-open**: when the touched-file set cannot be resolved, or any git call
   needed for the payload fails, return `None` (stale ⇒ re-run the pipeline).
5. **Tool artefacts**: choose and document one policy (see Open Question OQ1) —
   either an explicit ignore-list applied when building the path set, or
   documented always-invalidating behaviour with a test.
6. Preserve the legacy time gate for fingerprint-less reports and the
   persistence-write tolerance exactly as today.
7. Document the trade-offs: the gate is no longer "cheap fail-open"; tool-
   artefact rewrites may still invalidate; the safe direction remains
   stale ⇒ re-run.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Replace whole-repo `head_sha` +
  `working_tree_hash` with per-touched-path state in
  `_compute_content_fingerprint`; add a touched-file resolver (git log
  `--grep` + comment commit hashes + `_extract_key_files`); keep
  `_check_audit_freshness` / `_get_child_audit_verdict` comparison logic and
  fail-open behaviour.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — New/updated unit tests
  for AC1–AC4 and AC7 (unrelated commit, touched-file change, description
  change, fail-open, regression scenario).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Update the content-freshness description (L121) to
  the per-work-item touched-file semantics.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — Update the freshness sections (L231,
  L455, L605) and the tool-artefact policy.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT** (completed) — introduced the content-based freshness
  gate this item refines.
- **SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ** (open, `plan_complete`; commit `6910ad01` already in
  HEAD) — added whole-repo working-tree state to the fingerprint. Directly
  interacts with AC1/AC2: this item narrows that component to the touched-file
  set while retaining its stale-audit correctness property.
- **SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC** (completed) — "Eliminate wasteful re-audits"
  (parent concern).
- **SA-0MTFX6HMJ006QKR3** (completed) — freshness skip message surfacing
  verdict + timestamp.
- **SA-0MTFX6VD70097OEO** (completed) — second-audit short-circuit test
  (precedent for AC7).
- **SA-0MTJ0KO6L004GIZK** (open) — `--do-not-persist` leaves `auditedAt`
  stale; related resurfacing risk if the gate is narrowed.
- **SA-0MSL1Z70C007B9VZ** (open, `plan_complete`) — shared ISO-8601 freshness
  timestamp parsing; touch point in the same functions.
- **SA-0MSL1Z7E9005TLBA** (open) — reduce redundant `wl show` fetches during
  item audits; the new resolver must avoid adding redundant fetches.
- **SA-0MSP7P2PN009FT9U** (Nova repository) — the regression scenario behind
  AC7; not resolvable from this repository's worklog store.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM** – Audit staleness race: post-persist comment bumps updatedAt past auditedAt — passed audits show stale icon (completed)
- **SA-0MMQKV6L71FS6Q4N** – Restore Python runtime in AMPA pool review containers (completed)
- **SA-0MQWVU3A6007F38B** – Intake skill auto-complete leaves work-item as in_progress instead of open (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+161 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+151 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+131 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** the touched-file resolver could grow into a general
  git-history index. Mitigation: bound it to `--grep` on the item id + recorded
  commit hashes + Key Files; record anything further as a linked work item.
- **Risk (perf):** per-path git calls scale with the touched-file count.
  Mitigation: batch with a single `git log --name-only` where possible; cap the
  path count.
- **Risk (over-broad touched-file set):** `git log --grep=<id>` may match
  unrelated commits (e.g. a commit message mentioning the id). Mitigation:
  accept the safe direction (extra paths ⇒ more likely stale ⇒ re-run).
- **Risk (false freshness):** dropping the repo HEAD sha means a change to a
  genuinely-relevant file that is *not* in the resolved touched-file set would
  not invalidate. Mitigation: Key Files + recorded commits are unioned; any
  resolution failure fails open.
- **Assumption (A1):** "touched files" = union of commits referencing the item
  id (or recorded on its comments) and the description Key Files.
- **Assumption (A2):** the whole-repo `working_tree_hash` component is narrowed
  to the touched-file set rather than dropped, so uncommitted changes to
  touched files still invalidate.
- **Assumption (A3):** AC7 is satisfied by a repo-local regression test
  reproducing the scenario; the literal Nova item is not reachable here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **OQ1 (OPEN QUESTION — AC5 tool-artefact policy):** exclude a known
  tool-artefact ignore-list (e.g. Unity `ProjectSettings/**`, `*.meta`) from the
  touched-file set, or document them as always-invalidating with a test?
  **Interim assumption:** implement the documented always-invalidating
  behaviour with a test (safe default — no risk of missing a genuine change),
  and make the ignore-list a follow-up if producer prefers exclusions. Answer
  needed before implementing AC5 if exclusions are required.
  Source: pending producer input; derived from the work item's own AC5
  "either … or" wording.

- **OQ2 (OPEN QUESTION — AC7 reproducibility):** `NV-0MSP7P2PN009FT9U` belongs
  to the Nova repository's worklog store, which is not reachable from this
  checkout (`/mnt/u/Nova` absent; no `NV-` store resolvable). **Interim
  assumption:** reframe AC7 as a repo-local regression test that reproduces the
  scenario (unchanged touched-file state ⇒ stored verdict returned without
  model calls), as `SA-0MTFX6VD70097OEO` did for the previous gate. No answer
  needed to proceed; confirm if a live Nova re-audit is expected as acceptance
  evidence.
  Source: filesystem search for `NV-` worklog store; precedent
  `SA-0MTFX6VD70097OEO`.

- **OQ3 (RESOLVED BY AC1 — interaction with SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ):** that item
  is `plan_complete` yet its commit (`6910ad01`) is already an ancestor of HEAD.
  Its whole-repo working-tree component contradicts AC1 (unrelated working-tree
  changes must not invalidate), so it **must** be narrowed/absorbed here; there
  is no valid option that keeps it whole-repo. **Resolution:** narrow/absorb it
  into the per-touched-path payload and record the relationship, so the two do
  not ship competing fingerprint components.
  Source: `git log --all --grep=SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` (commit `6910ad01`);
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms it is in HEAD. Derivation: AC1 of this
  item.

## Goal

Fix `_run_eslint_findings_check` and `_run_eslint_fix_mode` in `linter_runner.py` to filter file targets to JS/TS extensions before invoking eslint, preventing false parsing errors on `.py` and other non-JS/TS files.

## Root Cause

- `_run_eslint_findings_check` (line 351): `cmd = ["eslint", *[str(f) for f in files], "-f", "json", "--quiet"]` passes raw `files` with no extension filter.
- `_run_eslint_fix_mode` (lines 722, 727): same gap in both `fix_cmd` and `rescan_cmd`.
- ESLint v6.4.0 tries to parse `.py` files as JavaScript and emits "Parsing error: Unterminated string constant".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Scoped eslint runs filter file targets to JS/TS extensions; a `.py`-only changed-file list produces zero eslint findings (eslint skipped or given no JS/TS targets).
- [ ] `_run_eslint_findings_check` filters `files` to JS/TS extensions (`.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.ts`, `.tsx`) before building the eslint command.
- [ ] `_run_eslint_findings_check` returns `[]` (skips eslint) when no JS/TS targets remain after filtering.
- [ ] `_run_eslint_fix_mode` filters both `fix_cmd` and `rescan_cmd` to JS/TS extensions only.

## Problem Statement

Agents repeatedly make the same mistakes when working with pi — using `skill_path` as a bash command instead of the tool, expanding backticks in shell commands, forgetting Python imports, and falling into self-correction loops. A skill that analyses recent session logs to detect these patterns would enable proactive skill improvements and prevent recurring failures.

## Users

- **Agent operator / PI** — receives a structured report of agent confusion patterns and actionable improvement recommendations.
- **Skill authors** — get targeted work items to update SKILL.md files, scripts, or add guardrails.
- **Producers** — understand systemic agent behaviour issues across the project.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Skill reads the last 20 session logs (`.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl`) for the CWD project, sorted by modification time.
2. Heuristic analysis extracts: tool call distribution, thinking-content error signals (keywords: error, fail, retry, incorrect, sorry, wrong, fix, correct, issue, problem, confused, wait, actually, oh, hmm, ah), tool result errors (tracebacks, permission denied, command not found, shell expansion errors), and retry/self-correction patterns.
3. LLM-assisted interpretation (via pi calls) classifies patterns into categories (e.g. "skill invocation confusion", "shell quoting issues", "Python import omissions", "permission issues") and generates recommendations.
4. Structured report rendered in the agent response with: summary of findings, top patterns by frequency, recommended skill improvements, and evidence citations (which sessions showed which patterns).
5. Recommendations are filed as worklog comments on the parent work item.
6. For each actionable recommendation, a child work item is auto-created with issue-type `chore` or `feature`, assigned to Map, and linked via `related-to:<parent-id>` in the description.
7. The skill follows existing project conventions: `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md`, `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/`, `skill/agent-log-review/tests/`.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md`).
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Hybrid approach: heuristics for extraction, LLM for classification — not fully automated LLM-only (too expensive) and not heuristic-only (too noisy).
- Only CWD project sessions; no cross-project analysis.
- Auto-create work items but don't implement them — that's downstream work.
- Must handle v3 session log format (session, model_change, thinking_level_change, message types with content as list of thinking/toolCall parts).

## Existing State

- Session logs exist at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl` in v3 format.
- Existing skills follow `SKILL.md` + `scripts/` + `tests/` convention.
- Related work: SA-0MSNYWMJJ002CIJ7 (tag pi sessions spawned from skills with `--session-id`), SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD (24h experiment: measure session length & token use), SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA and reliability recommendations for audit failures), SA-0MLGZN2IH0HH6JSH (Add 'waiting_for_input' session state).
- Known patterns already visible in current sessions: backtick expansion in bash commands, `skill_path` used as bash command, Python `NameError`/`KeyError` from missing imports, `python` vs `python3`, permission denied on script execution, self-correction loops in thinking content.

## Desired Change

A reusable skill that agents can invoke (e.g. `/skill:agent-log-review`) to periodically analyse session logs, produce reports, and auto-create improvement work items.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md` — skill definition and invocation docs
- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — main analysis script
- `skill/agent-log-review/tests/test_agent_log_review.py` — unit tests
- `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md` — skill reference docs

## Risks & Assumptions

**Assumptions**
- Pi v3 session log format is stable (fields: `session`, `model_change`, `thinking_level_change`, `message` with list content of `thinking`/`toolCall` parts, `toolResult` role).
- `<project-slug>` session directory is derived deterministically from CWD (e.g. `--home-rgardler-projects-SorraAgents--`).
- 20 sessions is a statistically useful sample size for common patterns.

**Risks & mitigations**
- **LLM cost/latency** — 20 logs total several MB; mitigate by sending only distilled heuristic signals (counts, excerpts) to the LLM, not raw logs.
- **False positives** — keyword heuristics over-trigger on legitimate uses of "error" (e.g. error-handling code). Mitigate with context windows and LLM confirmation before filing work items.
- **Huge individual sessions** — streaming line-by-line parse, cap per-session excerpt size.
- **Privacy** — session logs may contain paths/tokens; redact secrets in the report and never persist raw log content outside `.worklog/tmp/`.
- **Scope creep** — do not build auto-fix/auto-edit of skills; keep to report + work-item creation (extra opportunities become linked, not in-scope).

## Related work

- SA-0MSNYWMJJ002CIJ7 — Skills: tag pi sessions spawned from skills with --session-id (helps identify skill-spawned sessions for analysis)
- SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD — 24h experiment: AGENTS.md STE100 instruction — measure session length & token use vs previous period (analysis pattern)
- SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL — RCA and reliability recommendations: why audit Phase 1/Phase 2 frequently fail (similar RCA approach)
- SA-0MLGZN2IH0HH6JSH — Add 'waiting_for_input' session state (session analysis infrastructure)

- Q: "Analysis engine — what approach for pattern detection (heuristic only / LLM-assisted / hybrid)?" — Answer (operator): "hybrid". Source: interactive reply. Research: confirmed existing skills use pi calls (e.g. audit Phase 2) so LLM calls from a skill are an established pattern.
- Q: "Scope — which projects' logs, and where should the report go?" — Answer (operator): "the project from which the skill is initiated (CWD), recommendations filed in the worklog, report returned in agent response". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Recommendations — should the skill auto-create work items, or report-only?" — Answer (operator): "create". Source: interactive reply.

## Problem

The remote `dev` branch (github.com:SorraTheOrc/SorraAgents) was force-pushed to test-fixture commits, destroying the real dev history.

### Evidence

`gh api repos/SorraTheOrc/SorraAgents/commits?sha=dev` returned test-fixture commits:
- `1e24d155 Test main`
- `5e129a20 T init`
- `fe099f2c Test init`
- ... (~59 fixture commits)

The last legitimate dev commit was `6d7b4b4f` (feat(intake,plan): require explicit preferred option in interview skills, 2026-09-24T20:25+01:00).

### Root cause (preliminary)

Running `run_tests.py --scope full` from the main checkout mutated the main repo's `dev` branch HEAD (reflog filled with "Branch: renamed refs/heads/dev to refs/heads/dev") and the full suite appears to `git push` test fixtures to the real `origin/dev`. Fixture authors seen: `Test <test@test.com>`, `T <t@t.com>`, `Cache Test`, `RT Test`.

Suspected sources include `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` (creates `wl-OSL-1-test` worktree/branch) and `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` (creates `origin/dev` local branch) — both should be isolated in `tmp_path` but the real repo acquired branches `wl-OSL-1-test`, `feature-x`, `wl-SA-001-test-feature`.

### Impact

- Real dev history unreachable from the remote
- Any agent that fetched/cloned dev gets garbage
- Force-push required to restore

### Required fix

1. Identify the test(s) that mutate the real repo and/or push to the real remote; make them fully hermetic (set `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` sandbox, use `tmp_path` remotes, or `git -c` isolation).
2. Add a regression guard that fails if a test suite run changes the main repo's branch/refs.
3. Restore `dev` to `6d7b4b4f` + legitimate work.

### Restore action taken

Dev restored to `bbf76459` (6d7b4b4f + SA-0MTC5CRVI008RD1K install_pi fix) — pending verification.
